SMTO-GML-0031 — Google is limiting how fast SMTO can use Gmail

GUID: 459346a8-8ab8-4e9b-8a2e-44c1a654fa38
Slug: gmail-provider-rate-limited
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • Google temporarily refused this Gmail request because too many requests were made in a short time. That request was turned down, but earlier steps in the same Task may already be done.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait at least a few minutes before asking SMTO to use Gmail again, and don't keep repeating the request in the meantime. Every new attempt counts against Google's limit and can keep the block in place longer.
  2. If the Task was sending or changing emails, open Gmail in your browser and check which ones are already done. Some emails may have been sent or changed before Google started refusing requests.
  3. Ask again in the conversation with a smaller job, for example one label or one day of email at a time, and only for what is still missing. Smaller requests make fewer calls to Google, so they are less likely to hit the limit again.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finishes the Gmail request without this error, and each email or change appears in Gmail only once.

If it still fails

  • If it keeps happening for an hour or more, select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; they may need to check the Gmail usage limits in your organization's Google Cloud project. Don't set up repeated automatic retries.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Google answered a Gmail or Google sign-in request with HTTP 429 (rate or quota limit), and the error resolver classified the GmailApiError as a provider rate limit.

What this means

  • The resolver receives a typed GmailApiError with numeric status 429 and selects the provider rate-limit identity. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • The resolver receives a typed GmailApiError with numeric status 429 and selects the provider rate-limit identity.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the actual provider retry/quota evidence rather than selecting an arbitrary fixed delay.

How to fix it

  • The Gmail API or OAuth endpoint returned 429. Wait for the quota window to reset (reads already retry up to three attempts with 0.1 s and 0.2 s backoff), reduce request rate or batch size, and check the Gmail API per-user and project quota for the OAuth client in the Google Cloud console. Inspect existing operation results before resubmitting any write, and avoid tight retry loops.
  • Respect provider throttling and the existing bounded backoff policy.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • Later permitted requests respect provider retry guidance and existing bounded backoff.

What not to do

  • Do not use a rapid retry loop or replay an uncertain mutation while waiting for the stated condition.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
